subject.title: Cron sessions deliver hallucinated output instead of failing cleanly when tool calls fail

question: What cron/unattended finalization contract should OpenClaw enforce when failed, missing, or unverified tool work is followed by success-looking final assistant text?
rationale: The current code intentionally allows some final assistant text to recover warning/error paths, and changing that default affects security posture, operator trust, and compatibility for existing cron jobs.

options.title: Fail closed on unrecovered structured failures
options.body: Treat unattended runs with failed or missing required tool state as non-deliverable unless a later structured success proves recovery, while preserving verified recovery output.

options.title: Add opt-in strict mode first
options.body: Keep existing delivery behavior by default and introduce a documented strict cron policy so maintainers can measure over-suppression before changing defaults.

options.title: Keep generic claim checks in plugins only
options.body: Limit core to narrow fatal signals and leave broader success-claim verification to ClawHub plugins, accepting that this issue remains only partially addressed in cron core.

recommendation.title: Fail closed on unrecovered structured failures
recommendation.body: Treat unattended runs with failed or missing required tool state as non-deliverable unless a later structured success proves recovery, while preserving verified recovery output.

likelyOwner.reason: This is the strongest routing candidate because of recent adjacent agent-runtime hardening and the related #68051 plugin-scope decision.
